correctness.rationale: The domination cases are exhaustive by side occupancy. For \(n\ge3\), same-side distinct vertices have distance \(2\), nonmatched opposite-side vertices have distance \(1\), and matched opposite-side vertices have distance \(3\). Thus the semipartner graph of an even selected set is a complete graph with a matching removed; an explicit construction gives a perfect matching at every selected size at least \(4\). The only dominating two-sets are removed matching pairs and fail. Exhaustive checking confirms all subsets and coefficients for \(3\le n\le8\).

value.rationale: Semipaired domination is NP-complete even on bipartite graphs, so a complete exact solution on crown graphs is a natural structured benchmark. The theorem resolves every feasible subset and its cardinality distribution, not merely a minimum value. The deleted perfect matching creates a sharp interaction with the distance-two pairing rule: all ordinary size-two minima are excluded while every larger even dominating set becomes semipairable.
